subject: Helion Health: GPU family substitution & billing exception request
messages:
From: Sarah Mitchell <sarah.mitchell@helionhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Cc: purchases@helionhealth.com, rajiv.patel@helionhealth.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion

Thanks for the call this morning, Karthik. A couple of clarifications from our side: Helion is evaluating a three-quarter reserved program for 150 concurrent sessions (mostly inference-heavy pipelines) and we need H100-class accelerators due to our LLM variant and latency requirements. Your standard Dedicated SKU defaults to A100; the performance delta for our model is material.

Two asks so we can proceed to procurement:
- Formal confirmation that Redwood can deliver H100 family for the committed pool (or equivalent performance profile) and hold capacity during our internal approval window (we need a 60–90 day reservation hold).
- A one-time overage protection: because we run production spikes at month-end, we need capped overage rates (no more than 1.5x the committed unit rate) and a temporary burst buffer for 30 days following launch.

We have legal redlines (see attached) and will need to know whether pricing/terms are negotiable or need exec sign-off. If this requires an exception, please escalate and let us know what info you need (usage forecast, security artifacts, SOC2 evidence).

Best,
Sarah Mitchell
Head of Cloud Ops, Helion Health

Attachments: Helion_MSA_redlines.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
To: Sarah Mitchell <sarah.mitchell@helionhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion

Sarah — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the redlines. Appreciate the explicit performance requirement; H100 is not our default for new Dedicated deals but we do have a path to support it with a small hardware surcharge and a reservation hold.

Quick notes/questions for procurement so we can get the right approval:
- Can you share a 90-day rolling peak concurrency forecast (simple daily peak) so we can size the burst buffer? If not, the worksheet attached with your estimated 10/20/30-day peaks helps.
- Helion asked for capped overage at 1.5x committed rate — that is a non-standard overage band and will require deal-desk + finance sign-off.
- Reservation hold for 60–90 days: we can do a 90-day hold for H100 on a provisional basis but it will require an exec-level capacity exception and a waiver on the auto-scheduler that normally reclaims uncommitted reserved GPUs.

I'm escalating to Lauren and Marissa for explicit approval on three items: (1) H100 family substitution & temporary hardware surcharge, (2) 90-day reservation hold, and (3) capped overage at 1.5x for the first 3 months of production launch. See my quick summary below.

--- Summary for exec review ---
Customer: Helion Health (RD-4832)
Commit: 150 concurrent sessions, 36-month term (standard) but requesting early launch with 30-day burst and 90-day reservation hold
Requested exceptions:
  * GPU family: H100 (non-standard for new Dedicated pools)
  * Reservation hold: 90 days (prevent auto-reclaim)
  * Overage cap: 1.5x committed unit rate for first 3 months
Impact: Higher unit cost to Redwood (H100 allocation), potential short-term capacity pressure in region us-west-2 during Q4 launches, modest margin compression for first 3 months.
Recommended temporary mitigations: 1) apply 10% hardware surcharge on reserved units, 2) require DocuSign acceptance of a 90-day hold addendum, 3) require minimum committed run rate (monthly usage threshold) to trigger the capped overage.

I can attach the capacity worksheet and the draft addendum if that helps.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity-worksheet.xlsx
From: lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, aditya_rao@redwood-inference.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helion Health: GPU family substitution & billing exception request

Karthik — thanks for the concise summary. I reviewed the customer's redlines and your recommendation. A few points before I sign off or escalate to execs: 

1) Hardware & capacity: I'm provisionally comfortable approving H100 substitution with a 12% hardware surcharge for the reserved pool, provided Finance signs off on the margin plan and we attach a capacity-protection fee that is refundable if we can't provision H100 within 45 days. That reduces some downstream risk.

2) Reservation hold: I can approve a 60-day hold administratively. 90-day hold needs EVP sign-off because it blocks scheduler capacity longer than our standard maximum. If the customer signs a DocuSign addendum committing to minimum monthly spend during the hold, escalate could be avoided.

3) Overage cap: 1.5x is aggressive; I can approve a temporary 1.75x cap for the first billing quarter as a manager-level concession. Anything below that requires Chief Revenue Officer sign-off. We should document an automatic reversion to standard overage rates after the three-month window.

Next steps I need from you to finalize:
- Finalized 90-day vs 60-day decision from the customer; if they accept a 60-day hold with the spend commitment, we'll avoid exec.
- Updated capacity worksheet with daily peaks (attached earlier).
- Draft addendum + commercial summary for CFO review (please route to finance).

If Helion can accept 60 days + spend commitment + 12% surcharge, I will sign. If they insist on 90 days and 1.5x cap, please prepare an exec memo and I'll route to the EVP for approval.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Deal Desk & Pricing, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
To: Sarah Mitchell <sarah.mitchell@helionhealth.com>, purchases@helionhealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, aditya_rao@redwood-inference.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helion Health: GPU family substitution & billing exception request

Sarah — quick follow-up after internal review. We can offer two paths; please confirm which Helion prefers so we can finalize the SOW and routing: 

Option A (manager-approved, faster):
- H100 family reservation with 60-day hold
- 12% hardware surcharge on reserved units
- Overage cap at 1.75x for first 3 months
- DocuSign addendum with minimum monthly spend during hold

Option B (exec exception, slower):
- H100 family reservation with 90-day hold
- Waive hardware surcharge (or reduce to 6%) for the first 3 months
- Overage cap at 1.5x for first 3 months
- Requires EVP approval and then DocuSign addendum

If you can accept Option A, I will have legal and finance prepare the addendum and push to DocuSign within 48 hours. If you need Option B, please say so and we'll start the fast-track exec memo.

Appreciate the quick read — happy to hop on a 20-min call to close details.

Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0143
